meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Used in Jordanian speech with subjunctive forms like أأذيها ('hurt her') and يأذوا ('they hurt').

examples.trans: I didn't mean to hurt you.
They won't hurt anyone.

meanings.note: Common Levantine word (from Italian arma) for a shopfront sign.

examples.trans: The shop has a big sign outside.
I saw the blue sign above the door.

meanings.note: Agrees with the speaker's gender: a man says أنا آسف, a woman says أنا آسفة.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for the delay.
Sorry for the bother, sir.

meanings.note: Describes a place or thing that is safe; for people 'safe and sound' is سالم.

examples.trans: The neighbourhood here is safe at night.
These stairs are not safe for children.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: Exclamation when a puzzle clicks into place ('aha!').

examples.trans: Aha! Now I understand the whole story!
Aha, that is why you took the bus!

meanings.note: Spontaneous Levantine exclamation when bumping or twisting something.

examples.text: آي! زحلقت رجلي عن طرف الطبلية!
examples.trans: Ouch! My foot slipped off the edge of the low stool!

examples.text: آي، إبريق الشاي لسا سخن كتير!
examples.trans: Ow, the teapot is still super hot!

meanings.note: Reinforces negation ('not at all, never'): ما في زبدة أبدا ('no butter at all'), لا تقلق أبدا ('do not worry at all').

examples.trans: There is no butter in the fridge at all!
Do not worry at all, sir.

meanings.note: Covers transitive 'push someone away' (أبعدها عني) and the everyday imperative ابعدي ('step away').

examples.trans: Step out of my way.
I wanted to push her away from me.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأجر, بيأجر).

examples.trans: We do not usually rent out the attic.
We rented out all the rooms this week.

أجّل.gloss: to postpone; move to a later date

meanings.en: to postpone; move to a later date
meanings.note: Form II Jordanian verb; spoken text omits shadda (أجلت تذكرتي 'I postponed my ticket').

examples.trans: We moved the meeting to Wednesday morning.

examples.text: رامي أجل تذكرته عشان يحضر الافتتاح.
examples.trans: Rami moved his ticket so he could attend the opening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أحرف.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أحرف.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أحرف.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أحرف.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of منيح ('good'). Before a noun without ال- it means 'the best' (أحسن نومة 'the best sleep').

examples.trans: This is the best room in the house.
I feel better today.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of حلو ('sweet, lovely').

examples.trans: It has the loveliest view of the courtyard.
This is the nicest day of the week.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday adverb 'sometimes'.

examples.trans: Sometimes air gets into the pipes at night.
Sometimes we have tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective placed after a definite noun (السلم الأخير 'the final scale'). Feminine: أخيرة, plural: أخيرين.

examples.trans: This is the final scene in today's episode.
We played the final scale in complete calm.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of دافي ('warm'); also spelled أدفا.

examples.trans: The piano's sound is warmer when it rains.
The attic is the warmest room in winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أدلة.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أدلة.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أدلة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أدلة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أذكياء.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أذكياء.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أذكياء.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أذكياء.

meanings.note: Standard/polite word for 'ear' alongside colloquial ذان; feminine in agreement.

examples.text: قرب أذنك واسمع رنة الوتر الصافية.
examples.trans: Bring your ear close and listen to the clear ring of the string.

examples.text: مدام سعاد عندها أذن موسيقية ما بتخطئ نغمة.
examples.trans: Madam Suad has a musical ear that never misses a note.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أربع.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أربع.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أربع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أربع.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fourteen'.

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
It is seven fourteen.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Literally 'I beg/hope of you'. Uses -ak/-ik/-kum endings depending on whom you address (أرجوكي to a woman, أرجوكم to a group).

examples.trans: Please let me write the new label!
Please wait a moment by the door.

meanings.note: Collective noun for cedar wood or cedar trees.

examples.trans: This is an old cedar wood box.
The scent of cedar wood is very pleasant.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite having no -a ending; means ground, land, or indoor floor.

examples.trans: The floor is clean and dry now.
Set the box on the floor for a moment.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أرضية, plural: أرضيين).

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the ground floor.
The ground-floor rooms are close to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: أرضيات.

examples.trans: The floorboards are old and sturdy.
We wiped the floor in the morning.

meanings.note: Elative of رقيق ('delicate, thin'); in exclamations after ما (ما أرق هاللحن! 'how gentle this melody is!') it stays invariable.

examples.trans: How gentle the sound of the piano is at night!

examples.text: هاد الورق أرق من ورق الدفتر.
examples.trans: This paper is thinner than notebook paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بزعج, بيزعج).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
Sorry if we disturbed you at night.

meanings.note: In everyday Amman speech, أزمة most often means heavy city traffic.

examples.trans: Downtown traffic at noon is slow.
We arrived ten minutes before the traffic jam.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أستاذك.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أستاذك.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أستاذك.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أستاذك.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of سيئ ('bad').

examples.trans: The news is worse than we expected.
This is the worst time for rain.

meanings.note: Primary colour adjective ('black'); feminine and non-human plural form is سودا (sooda).

examples.text: جيب لفة لزاق أسود من الدكان.
examples.trans: Pick up a roll of black tape from the shop.
The black cat is sleeping under the tree.

meanings.note: Form IV verb paired with على ('supervise / oversee a task').

examples.text: سلمى بتشرف عالمطبخ وهي قاعدة عالكرسي.
examples.trans: Salma supervises the kitchen while sitting in her chair.

examples.text: أبو طارق أشرف على تركيب الشيش الأخضر.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq oversaw the installation of the green shutters.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أشوفكم.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أشوفكم.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أشوفكم.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أشوفكم.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أشياء.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أشياء.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أشياء.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أشياء.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأشر, بيأشر).

examples.trans: Salma motioned to me from the kitchen.
Rami is pointing to the two chairs.

أصبح.gloss: to wake in the morning; become (تصبحوا على خير good night)

meanings.en: to wake in the morning; become (تصبحوا على خير good night)
meanings.note: Used nightly in the warm Levantine farewell تصبحوا على خير ('may you wake in goodness' = good night).

examples.text: تصبحوا على خير يا جماعة، منشوفكم الصبح!
examples.trans: Good night, everyone—we'll see you in the morning!

examples.text: تصبح على خير يا عمي، ارتاح الليلة.
examples.trans: Good night, uncle, get some rest tonight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أصدقاء.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أصدقاء.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أصدقاء.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أصدقاء.

meanings.note: Comparative/superlative elative of صغير ('small/young'); invariant in spoken comparative use.

examples.text: تحت الاسم كتبنا السطر التاني بحروف أصغر.
examples.trans: Underneath the name we painted the second line in smaller letters.

examples.text: المرتبان الأصغر مخصص لملح البحر الخشن.
examples.trans: The smaller jar is reserved for coarse sea salt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صفرا, plural: صفر).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.
The yellow lemon cake is ready.

أصلا.gloss: anyway; in the first place; actually

meanings.en: anyway; in the first place; actually
meanings.note: Everyday conversational adverb meaning 'in the first place / anyway / to begin with'.

examples.trans: Does the attic even have a comfortable bed?
The wire needed adjusting anyway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أصلية, plural: أصليين).

examples.trans: The ceiling is solid oak wood.
All the old tilework is original.

meanings.note: Praises honest natural materials, authentic recipes, or trustworthy character.

examples.text: الخشب الأصيل بيعيش سنين طويلة لو اعتنينا فيه.
examples.trans: Honest solid wood lasts for decades when cared for.

examples.text: قائمة سلمى بسيطة وأصيلة من خيرات البلد.
examples.trans: Salma's menu is simple and authentic, made with local produce.

meanings.note: Form IV hollow verb (بضيف / ضفت). Used for adding an item to a box, list, or recipe.

examples.text: كل واحد بيضيف تذكار صغير للعلبة.
examples.trans: Everyone adds one small keepsake to the tin.
We added a little honey and orange zest.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of طويل ('tall, long').

examples.trans: You have grown taller than the piano!
The bridge route is two minutes longer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of غريب ('strange').

examples.trans: The story gets stranger every hour.
That is the strangest request I have heard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective.

examples.trans: Guests wake up early for the most part.
Most houses here are made of stone.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; the plural أغاني (aghaani) is the one you hear most.

examples.trans: This is an old song my grandmother loves.
We listen to songs in the car every morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أقرأ.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أقرأ.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أقرأ.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أقرأ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective.

examples.trans: At least the bread is ready in the oven.
We need less than ten minutes.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of أكثر ('more, most').

examples.trans: I liked working here much more.
Who knows the neighbourhood better than you?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باكل, بياكل).

examples.trans: The brothers are eating lemon cake in the courtyard.
We ate a hot breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Means 'certainly, definitely' or 'must be' (إنتي أكيد نور 'you must be Nour').

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.

examples.text: أكيد صاحبه رح يدور عليه قريبا.
examples.trans: Surely its owner will look for it soon.

meanings.note: In بحسب إلها ألف حساب ('counts a thousand accounts for her'), ألف intensifies caution: everyone thinks twice around her.

examples.trans: I thought about it a thousand times.
Thanks a thousand times.

ألقى.gloss: to cast; take (ألقي نظرة take a look)

meanings.en: to cast; take (ألقي نظرة take a look)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلقي, بيلقي).

examples.trans: Let me take a look at the letter.
He took a quick look at the ledger.

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian way to answer or check a phone line.

examples.trans: Hello? Jasmine House, how may I help you?
Hello, can you hear me clearly?

meanings.note: With 1sg suffix أمي (ummi), affectionately means 'Mom' even when talking to a sibling ('our mom').

examples.text: أمي علمتني أعمل شوربة عدس بالليمون.
examples.trans: Mom taught me how to make lentil soup with lemon.

examples.text: كل جمعة بنزور بيت أمي بعمان.
examples.trans: Every Friday we visit my mom's house in Amman.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from أمام ('in front of'): الغرفة الأمامية / الباب الأمامي.

examples.text: علقنا اللوحة الجديدة جنب البوابة الأمامية.
examples.trans: We hung the new sign beside the front gate.
The front windows look straight out onto the lane.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Safety in the house is very important.
They arrived safely and securely.

meanings.note: Means something kept in trust for someone, and in Amman also names City Hall (أمانة عمان).

examples.trans: I have something entrusted for you from your grandfather.
We put the bag in the left-luggage closet.

meanings.note: Plural أوامر means 'orders / instructions' (أوزع أوامر 'hand out orders').

examples.text: الشيف سلمى جاهزة توزع أوامر عالفريق كله!
examples.trans: Chef Salma is ready to issue orders to the whole team!

examples.text: تحت أمرك يا معلم، الشيش صار جاهز للتركيب.
examples.trans: At your service, boss—the shutters are ready to mount.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أنوف.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your nose now.
The air feels cold on my nose in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقذ, بينقذ).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
You saved my whole trip.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of هادي ('quiet, calm').

examples.trans: Jasmine House is the calmest place in Amman.
The street is much quieter at night.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun meaning 'family/parents' or 'people of a place' (يا أهل شارع الياسمين 'friends/folks of Jasmine Street').

examples.trans: Welcome to the friends of Jasmine Street!
My family comes to visit me every Friday.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Elative form placed before a definite plural noun (أهم القيم 'the most important values').

examples.trans: This is the most important topic today.
Honesty is the most important thing.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: Lighthearted exclamation after a small spill or slip.

examples.trans: Oops! A drop of juice landed on my tie!
Oops, I left the pen on the desk.

meanings.note: Elative comparative of واطي ('low'). Invariable for gender and number before or after nouns.

examples.trans: Put the chair on the lowest step.
This shelf is lower than the window.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Musical interval of eight scale steps.

examples.text: مدام سعاد عزفت نفس اللحن أوكتاف أعلى.
examples.trans: Madam Suad played the same melody one octave higher.

examples.text: الأوكتاف الوسطاني بالبيانو بده دوزان بسيط.
examples.trans: The middle octave on the piano needs a light tuning.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة أولى.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing أولى.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على أولى.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with أولى.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Jordan, Syria, Lebanon and Palestine use the old Syriac-derived month names: كانون التاني January ... أيار May ... أيلول September.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'when?'.

examples.trans: When does the hardware shop open?
When did the bus arrive at the station?

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmation ('yes! / exactly!').

examples.text: أيوا، هاد هو اللحن اللي كنت أدور عليه!
examples.trans: Yes, that's the exact melody I was looking for!

examples.text: أيوا بالزبط، حط الكراسي جنب القوس.
examples.trans: Yes, right there—put the chairs beside the arch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أباريق.

examples.trans: The teapot is hot on the table.
Pour the hot water into the teapot.

meanings.note: Used in تحت إبطي ('tucked under my arm') when carrying books or newspapers.

examples.text: مازن كان حامل الدفتر الأخضر تحت إبطه.
examples.trans: Mazen was carrying the green ledger under his arm.

examples.text: حط الجريدة تحت إبطه ومشي عالسوق.
examples.trans: He tucked the newspaper under his arm and walked to the market.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun for 'we' (equivalent to formal نحن).

examples.trans: We respect all our guests.
We are ready for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Used constantly in the polite phrase عن إذنك ('excuse me / with your permission').

examples.trans: Excuse me, may I pass?
He asked permission before heading out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for the disturbance.
There is no bother at all.

meanings.note: Soft cleaning sponge for washing windows or dishes.

examples.text: اعصري الإسفنجة منيح قبل ما تمسحي القزاز.
examples.trans: Wring the sponge out well before wiping the glass.
We bought two new sponges for the café kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: إشعارات.

examples.trans: An official notice arrived in the mail.
I read the notice twice.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a finger or toe; dual إصبعين ('two fingers'), broken plural أصابع.

examples.trans: Pull the paper out gently with two fingers.

examples.text: خلي أصابعك بعيدة عن الفرن السخن.
examples.trans: Keep your fingers away from the hot oven.

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian noun for a picture frame (إطار الجوز 'walnut frame') or tyre. Plural: إطارات.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة جوا إطار جوز حلو.
examples.trans: We placed the map inside a lovely walnut frame.
This wooden frame protects the drawing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: إطلالات.

examples.trans: The room has a lovely view onto the courtyard.
This is the prettiest view in the house.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine dative base taking pronoun endings: إلي (to me), إلك (to you), إلها (to her), إلنا (for us), إلهم (to them).

examples.trans: This book is for you.
Tell me the truth.

meanings.note: Means 'except / unless' (إلا إذا 'unless') and 'minutes to the hour' (اطنعش إلا خمسة 'five to twelve').

examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve!

examples.text: ما حدا بيقيس الساحة إلا مهندس!
examples.trans: Nobody measures a courtyard except an engineer!

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine form of أم ('mother'); إمي means 'my mother'.

examples.text: إمي بتعمل أطيب مربى مشمش بالصيف.
examples.trans: My mother makes the best apricot jam in summer.

examples.text: سلم على إمك لما ترجع عالبيت.
examples.trans: Say hello to your mother when you get home.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one man.

examples.trans: Did you plant these herbs yourself?
Did you plan this entire meeting?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.trans: You must be Nour!
You are today's heroine, Nour.

examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing إنش.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على إنش.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with إنش.

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmative particle alongside آه and نعم.

examples.trans: He nodded his head yes.

meanings.note: Carries a direct-object pronoun after pseudo-verbs like بدي: اللي بدك إياه ('whatever you want [it]').

examples.trans: Take whatever you want.
I gave it to you yesterday.

examples.trans: That is exactly what I want.
I gave it to you this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: إيجارات.

examples.trans: The shop rent is paid until summer.
We signed the lease today.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Musical rhythm or tempo pattern.

examples.text: إيقاع الفالس خفيف وبيرقص متل الموج.
examples.trans: A waltz rhythm is light and swaying like waves.

examples.text: دقت سعاد الإيقاع بأصابعها على طرف الطاولة.
examples.trans: Suad tapped the rhythm with her fingers on the edge of the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine question word for 'when?' (alongside متى).

examples.text: إيمتى رح نعلق الشيش الأخضر عالشبابيك؟
examples.trans: When are we going to hang the green shutters on the windows?

examples.text: إيمتى بيجهز أول فوج خبز الصبح؟
examples.trans: When does the first batch of bread come out in the morning?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببتسم, بيبتسم).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
He smiled when he saw his brother.

meanings.note: Combines with عم ('paternal uncle') as ابن عمي ('my cousin').

examples.text: ابن عمي ساكن قريب من هون.
examples.trans: My cousin lives near here.
The boys are playing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of اتجه. With بـ, باتجاه means 'toward' (باتجاه الشباك 'toward the window').

examples.trans: He raised his cup toward the room's window.
He pointed us in the direction of the bus station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصل, بيتصل).

examples.trans: Call the lost-and-found office right away.
You called us on Tuesday.

meanings.note: Used when reminding friends of what they agreed on (مش هيك الاتفاق 'that wasn't the deal').

examples.trans: That was our deal from the start.
We reached a clear agreement.

meanings.note: Said on its own, اتفقنا ('we agreed') is the everyday way to close a deal: 'deal!'.

examples.text: اتفقنا، بنلتقي الساعة تسعة عند الباب.
examples.trans: Agreed, we meet at nine at the door.

examples.text: اتفقت مع سلمى على كيكة الجمعة.
examples.trans: I agreed with Salma about the Friday cake.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian for 12. From eleven up, the counted noun stays singular: اتنعش فنجان 'twelve cups'.

examples.trans: We have twelve guests tonight.
It's twelve noon.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb taking بـ for what is celebrated.

examples.trans: We're going to celebrate the café opening with all the neighbours.

examples.text: احتفلنا لما خلص دهان الشيش قبل المغرب.
examples.trans: We celebrated when the shutter painting finished before dusk.

meanings.note: Often placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'spare' (مفتاح احتياط a spare key).

examples.trans: I have a spare key in the drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستاهل, بيستاهل).

The house is worth all this effort.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian Form X verb (بيستاهل / بتستاهل) meaning 'to deserve, be worth it'.

examples.trans: The ovens deserve a break after baking!

examples.text: انتي بتستاهلي كل خير يا سلمى.
examples.trans: You deserve every good thing, Salma.

meanings.note: Both a quiet personal breather (تاخدي استراحة) and school recess.

meanings.note: Levantine passive Form VII of حط ('to put/place').

examples.trans: The new tables were placed under the arch.
The green ledger was put away in the attic chest.

انحل.gloss: to dissolve; come untied; be solved

meanings.en: to dissolve (in water); to be solved or untied
meanings.note: Form VII medio-passive of حل ('to untie / solve'). Used for ink running in water or a knot coming undone.

examples.trans: Blue ink dissolves quickly in water.
The problem was solved calmly.

meanings.note: Form VII Medio-passive of دفع ('to pay'): اندفع حقه means 'its price has been paid'.

examples.trans: The bill was paid in cash at the desk.
Everything was paid for at the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects old houses.
Amman has beautiful architectural heritage.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تراثية, plural: تراثيين).

examples.trans: He works on restoring heritage buildings in Amman.

examples.text: هاد بيت تراثي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: This is a historic house eighty years old.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رتّب ('to tidy, arrange'); بترتيب means 'neatly, in neat order'.

examples.trans: We lined the chairs up neatly beside the wall.

examples.text: ترتيب الطاولات بالساحة ما أخد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Arranging the tables in the courtyard did not take ten minutes.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ترحيب ('welcoming'). Feminine: ترحيبية (لوحة ترحيبية 'welcome sign').

examples.text: كتبنا لوحة ترحيبية للضيف قبل ما يوصل.
examples.trans: We wrote a welcome sign for the guest before he arrived.
A welcoming smile is the most important thing at the front desk.

meanings.note: Form V verb meaning 'be promoted to a higher post or role'.

examples.text: نور ترقت وصارت موظفة استقبال رسمية.
examples.trans: Nour got promoted to permanent receptionist.
We got promoted today to café taste testers!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة تستنى.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing تستنى.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تستنى.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تستنى.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'nineteen' before a counted noun.

examples.trans: I wrote nineteen reasons on the sheet!
He is nineteen years old.

تشرّف.gloss: to be honoured (تشرفنا nice to meet you)

meanings.en: to be honoured (تشرفنا nice to meet you)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتشرف, بيتشرف).

examples.trans: Lovely to meet you, Salma!
I am honoured to have met you all.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصالح, بيتصالح).

examples.trans: Thank goodness the two brothers finally made peace!
We reconciled and drank tea together.

meanings.note: Used with manner phrases like بشكل طبيعي ('in a normal way') or بطبيعتك ('naturally').

examples.trans: I acted calmly in front of everyone.
Act naturally.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة تضل.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing تضل.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تضل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تضل.

meanings.note: Core Levantine verb for 'look (at)' taking على or في.

examples.text: تطلعي من الشباك شوفي لون الشيش الأخضر!
examples.trans: Look out the window and see the green colour of the shutters!

examples.text: ليش بتطلعوا علي هيك؟ هلا بمسح الدهان!
examples.trans: Why are you staring at me like that? I'll wipe the paint right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة تطلعوا.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing تطلعوا.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تطلعوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تطلعوا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تطورات.

examples.trans: That is excellent progress at work.
We heard the latest developments in the morning.

meanings.note: An imperative-only word: تعال to a man, تعالي to a woman, تعالوا to a group. Other tenses use إجا.

examples.trans: Come and sit next to me.
Come to the kitchen, all of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة تعالوا.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing تعالوا.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تعالوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تعالوا.

meanings.note: Universal everyday Jordanian adjective for 'tired' (feminine: تعبانة, plural: تعبانين).

examples.text: أنا تعبان شوي من رحلة الباص الطويلة.
examples.trans: I am a little tired from the long bus trip.

examples.text: صوتي تعبان اليوم، بس قلبي فرحان.
examples.trans: My voice is tired today, but my heart is glad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تعديلات.

examples.trans: The old wire needs a small adjustment.
We made a small adjustment to the schedule.

meanings.note: Wooden or iron garden trellis supporting climbing jasmine, grapevines, or ivy.

examples.text: رفعنا عرق اللبلاب شوي شوي عالتعريشة.
examples.trans: We lifted the ivy vine gently onto the trellis.

examples.text: القعدة تحت تعريشة الياسمين بالصيف بترد الروح.
examples.trans: Sitting under the jasmine trellis in summer refreshes the soul.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتعرف, بيتعرف).

examples.text: هادي كانت خطتي قبل ما أتعرف عليكم.
examples.trans: That was my plan before I got to know you all.
We met kind neighbours in the quarter.

meanings.note: Form V passive/intransitive counterpart to علّق ('to hang something up').

examples.trans: The lantern will hang above the door.
The sign was hung in the hall.

meanings.note: Form V reflexive of علّم ('to teach').

examples.text: نور بتتعلم شغل الاستقبال بسرعة كبيرة.
examples.trans: Nour is learning the front-desk work very quickly.
I learned to play the piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of عيّن ('to appoint, hire to a post').

examples.text: فرحنا كتير بخبر تعيين نور بالنزل.
examples.trans: We were delighted at the news of Nour's permanent appointment at the inn.
The manager signed the appointment letter in the morning.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of غلّف ('to wrap/package'). ورق تغليف means 'wrapping paper'.

examples.text: فكينا ورق التغليف البني عن اللوحة.
examples.trans: We removed the brown wrapping paper from the painting.
Good wrapping keeps cake fresh.

meanings.note: Form V intransitive counterpart to غيّر ('to change something').

examples.trans: The appointment changed a moment ago.
The weather changes quickly in spring.

meanings.note: Expresses being caught off guard (بدل ما أتفاجأ هيك 'instead of being surprised like this').

examples.trans: I was surprised when I saw you here.
Don't be surprised by the news.

meanings.note: Collective تفاح ('apples'), singulative تفاحة ('an apple').

examples.trans: I bought red apples from the shop.
Apple jam is delicious at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة تفتح.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing تفتح.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تفتح.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تفتح.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة تفتحوا.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing تفتحوا.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تفتحوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تفتحوا.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of فتّش ('to inspect, check officially').

examples.text: لجنة التفتيش من البلدية جاية يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: The inspection team from City Hall is coming on Wednesday.
The whole kitchen is clean and ready for inspection.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتفرج, بيتفرج).

examples.trans: Nobody gawks at the guests here!

examples.text: كنت ناوي تتفرج من الشارع المقابل؟
examples.trans: Were you planning to watch from across the street?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة تفضلي.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing تفضلي.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تفضلي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تفضلي.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتفقد, بيتفقد).

examples.text: أنا بس بتفقد الطقس من الشباك!
examples.trans: I am just checking the weather from the window!
Tariq checked on the heater in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Quick thinking solved the problem.
That is smart, logical thinking.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Add the green mint right before serving.
The presentation is neat and lovely.

meanings.note: Form V verb; passive/reflexive of قدّم ('serve food/drink').

examples.text: الشوربة السخنة بتتقدم مع خبز محمص.
examples.trans: The hot soup is served with toasted bread.

examples.text: قهوة الصبح بتتقدم بالساحة الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Morning coffee is served in the courtyard at eight.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun for a written or official report (تقرير التراث 'the heritage report'). Plural: تقارير.

examples.text: تقرير البلدية مدح ساحتنا يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: The city report praised our courtyard on Wednesday.

examples.text: كتبت تقرير مختصر عن حالة المبنى.
examples.trans: I wrote a brief report on the condition of the building.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of قسم; تقسيم الغرف refers to the school-trip room assignments.

examples.trans: I didn't like the group assignments.
The room assignment list is ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة تقيلة.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing تقيلة.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تقيلة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تقيلة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تقييمات.

examples.trans: The guests wrote an excellent review.
We read all the reviews on the page.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian Form II verb from تقيل ('heavy'), matching Classical ثقّل.

examples.trans: Do not weigh the basket down with items.
Water weighs cloth down a lot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة تلات.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing تلات.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تلات.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تلات.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تلاجات.

examples.trans: The cold milk is inside the fridge.
Open the fridge and check the butter.

meanings.note: Small hill (plural تلال tilaal); familiar across hilly Amman.

examples.text: عمان مبنية على تلال حلوة بتطل عالسما.
examples.trans: Amman is built across lovely hills looking out at the sky.

examples.text: لما نقسم الشغل الكبير لتلال صغيرة بصير سهل.
examples.trans: When we break a big job into small hills, it becomes easy.

تلت.gloss: one third; twenty minutes (past the hour)

meanings.en: one third; twenty minutes (past the hour)
meanings.note: In Jordanian time-telling, وتلت means 'twenty past' (a third of an hour = 20 minutes): حدعش وتلت ('11:20').

examples.trans: It is twenty past eleven right now.
We arrived at twenty past eight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تلوج.

examples.trans: The water is cold as ice.
Snow fell on the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تليفونات.

examples.trans: The phone rang on the reception desk.
I wrote the phone number in the notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for mouth, or the pouring spout of a pitcher/teapot.

examples.trans: The pitcher's spout is a little wide.
He laughed wholeheartedly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian all-purpose word for 'all set, fine, spot-on!'.

examples.trans: Everything has to be spot-on!
Alright, I can remember the sentences.

meanings.note: Adverb 'exact, completely, perfectly'.

examples.trans: Its size fits you perfectly.
The street is completely empty at noon.

meanings.note: Intensifies similarity or agreement: متلكم تماماً ('just like you').

examples.trans: I know exactly what you mean.
I agree with you completely.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eighty'.

examples.text: خشب بلوط أصلي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: Solid oak wood eighty years old.
This house has lived through eighty winters!

meanings.en: to sway back and forth gently
meanings.note: Form VI verb from مال ('to lean / tilt'), expressing gentle rhythmic swaying.

examples.trans: The branches sway with the breeze.
The lanterns are swaying calmly.

meanings.note: Form V verb taking على for practicing music or a craft.

examples.trans: Can I practice the whole song on the piano?

examples.text: مدام سعاد تمرنت ساعة كاملة قبل شاي المساء.
examples.trans: Madam Suad practiced for a full hour before evening tea.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of مرّن ('to train / practice'). Plural: تمارين.

examples.trans: We have piano rehearsal at four o'clock.
This exercise is easy and useful.

meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb without أن in spoken Arabic (بتتمنى تكون 'wishes to be').

examples.trans: I hope we'll be in the same class.
Every girl wishes to succeed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتمنى, بيتمنى).

examples.trans: We hope every guest feels comfortable with us.
We wished them a happy trip.

meanings.en: harmony; moving or sounding in unison
meanings.note: Built from نغمة ('musical note / tone'). Used for music, colours, or coordinated motion.

examples.trans: The lanterns move in lovely harmony.
There is clear harmony in the playing.

meanings.note: Form V verb from نفس ('breath').

examples.text: فتحت الشباك عشان أتنفس هوا نضيف.
examples.trans: I opened the window to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: بعد ما رتبنا القائمة، قدرت أتنفس براحة.
examples.trans: Once we organized the list, I could breathe easily.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'two' (إنتو التنين 'the two of you'); note homograph التنين ('Monday').

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: توائم.

examples.trans: The two suitcases are just like twins.
His twin brother lives next to him.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake turned out delicious!
We have an old mulberry tree in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتوتر, بيتوتر).

examples.trans: When I get nervous, my sentences turn long!

examples.text: لا تتوتر، كل شي رح يمشي تمام.
examples.trans: Do not get nervous, everything will go fine.

meanings.note: Loanword from English, for toasted sliced bread.

examples.trans: Do you want toast with the cheese?
The toast burned a little.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of وصّل ('to deliver, drop off; connect wires'); سيارة توصيل means 'delivery van'.

examples.trans: The delivery van pulled up in front of the gate.

examples.text: التوصيل للبيت مجاني إذا طلبنا دزينة.
examples.trans: Home delivery is free if we order a dozen.

meanings.note: Verbal noun from و-ف-ق; بالتوفيق! is the everyday Arabic way to say 'good luck!'.

examples.trans: Good luck in your new job, Nour!
Wish us luck before the municipality visit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتوفى, بيتوفى).

examples.trans: My grandfather passed away three years ago.

examples.text: ترك ذكرى طيبة بعد ما توفى.
examples.trans: He left warm memories after passing away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تواقيع.

examples.text: الورقة ما عليها اسم ولا توقيع.
examples.trans: The paper has neither name nor signature.
The postman asked for my signature.

meanings.note: Affectionate Levantine family word for 'grandmother' (often used directly without a possessive suffix).

examples.text: وصفة شوربة العدس هاي تعلمتها من تيتا.
examples.trans: I learned this lentil soup recipe from my grandma.

examples.text: تيتا دايما بتحط قشر ليمون طازة مع الكيك.
examples.trans: Grandma always puts fresh lemon zest into her cakes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ثواني.

examples.trans: Wait one second, please.
He came back ten seconds later on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بثبت, بيثبت).

examples.trans: Hold still a moment and listen to that sound!

examples.text: الكرسي ثبت بعد ما شدينا البرغي.
examples.trans: The chair held firm once we tightened the screw.

ثبّت.gloss: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place

meanings.en: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place
meanings.note: Form II verb meaning 'seat securely / hold steady'.

examples.text: طارق ثبت اللوحة النحاس ببراغي صغار.
examples.trans: Tariq fastened the brass plate with small screws.

examples.text: امسك السلم من تحت وثبته منيح.
examples.trans: Hold the ladder at the bottom and steady it well.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ثلاثين.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة ثمانية.

examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ثمانية.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Describes dry air, dry ingredients, or seasoned dry timber.

examples.text: خلينا نخلي كل المكونات الجافة عالرف العالي.
examples.trans: Let's keep all the dry ingredients on the upper shelf.

examples.text: المفصل بعد ما تدهنه زيت ما بيعود جاف.
examples.trans: Once you oil the hinge, it won't be dry anymore.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جاكيتات.

examples.trans: The key is in the right jacket pocket.

examples.text: البس جاكيت دافي قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Put on a warm jacket before you go out.

meanings.note: Feminine plural جامدات also appears in Jordanian speech for firm fruit (متل ليمونات جامدات).

examples.text: نقي ليمونات صفر وجامدات عشان تارت الليمون.
examples.trans: Pick firm yellow lemons for the lemon tarts.

examples.text: الكريمة بردت بالبراد وصارت جامدة ومتماسكة.
examples.trans: The curd chilled in the fridge and turned firm and set.

meanings.note: Relative adjective (nisba) from جانب ('side'), e.g. الباب الجانبي ('the side door'), القفل الجانبي ('the side latch').

examples.text: افتح الشباك الجانبي عشان يفوت الهوا.
examples.trans: Open the side window so fresh air comes in.

examples.text: في ممر جانبي صغير ورا المطبخ.
examples.trans: There is a small side passage behind the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جبانة, plural: جبناء).

examples.trans: It was a cowardly plan of mine.
Do not be timid, speak honestly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة جبت.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing جبت.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على جبت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with جبت.

meanings.note: Means 'mountain' and also names Amman's historic hilltop quarters (جبل اللويبدة, جبل عمان).

examples.text: الهوا على راس الجبل دايما نضيف ومنعش.
examples.trans: The air on top of the mountain is always clean and crisp.

examples.text: بيت الياسمين قريب من درج الجبل القديم.
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is near the old Jabal stairway.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from جبل ('mountain'); عسل جبلي ('mountain honey') is dark, aromatic wildflower honey.

examples.text: العسل الجبلي لونه غامق وطعمه غني.
examples.trans: Mountain honey has a dark colour and a rich taste.
The mountain air in Amman cools down at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: أجبان.

examples.trans: White cheese is tasty with mint.
We bought cheese and olives for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجبنة.

examples.trans: Your glasses are pushed up on your forehead!
He wiped the rain off his forehead.

meanings.note: Means 'grandfather' (جدي my grandfather) and in عن جد ('really / seriously') means 'earnestness'.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.
Did you really finish all the work?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جداول.

examples.trans: I read the bus timetable at the station.
The week's schedule is neat and clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة جربي.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing جربي.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على جربي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with جربي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجراس.

examples.trans: The gate bell rang twice.
Listen to the sound of the bell in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جريئة, plural: جريئين).

examples.text: الأخ الكبير كان جريء وصوته عالي.
examples.trans: The older brother was bold and loud-voiced.
A bold and excellent idea!

meanings.note: Everyday word for a newspaper; broken plural in spoken Levantine is جرايد (jaraayid).

examples.text: عمي بيقرا الجريدة مع فنجان قهوة كل صبح.
examples.trans: My uncle reads the newspaper with a cup of coffee every morning.

examples.text: لف البياع الصحون بورق جرايد قديم.
examples.trans: The seller wrapped the plates in old newspaper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجزاء.

examples.trans: This is the sweetest part of the story.
I read the first part of the book.

meanings.note: Collective noun جزر ('carrots') with singulative جزرة ('one carrot').

examples.text: فرمنا الجزر والبصل لمكعبات صغيرة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: We diced the carrots and onions into small, even cubes.

examples.text: الجزر المشوي بيعطي الشوربة حلاوة طبيعية.
examples.trans: Roasted carrots give the soup a natural sweetness.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جسور.

examples.trans: Cross the overpass toward downtown.
The old shop is past the overpass.

meanings.note: Verbal/abstract noun from جف ('become dry').

examples.text: الخشب بالبيانو بيحب جو معتدل ومش رطوبة شديدة.
examples.trans: Piano wood likes moderate air rather than extreme dampness or dryness.

examples.text: جفاف الهوا بعمان بيساعد الدهان ينشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: The dryness of Amman's air helps the paint dry fast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جلود.

examples.trans: This is a small brown leather notebook.
The leather bag is heavy and sturdy.

meanings.note: Craftsman's term for a small protective felt, rubber, or leather ring/bushing inside hardware or instruments.

examples.text: غيرنا جلدة اللباد الصغيرة تحت المفتاح فاختفت الطقة.
examples.trans: We replaced the tiny felt bushing under the key and the click vanished.

examples.text: شديت الصامولة بعد ما ركبت جلدة جديدة.
examples.trans: I tightened the nut after fitting a new washer.

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian way to greet a room: صباح الخير يا جماعة! ('Good morning, everyone!').

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
Come in, folks, the tea is ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Look at the beauty of the wooden ceiling!
The beauty of old stone rests the eye.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجمع, بيجمع).

examples.trans: Today our courtyard brings a family together!
We gathered the chairs under the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمع.

examples.trans: Every Friday morning we drink coffee.
Friday is a lovely day in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمل.

examples.trans: Start with three short, simple sentences.
Write this sentence in the notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'next to, beside'.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guests arrived from the south in the morning.
The weather is warm in the south today.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a garden or yard; a small one is a جنينة, the formal word is حديقة.

examples.trans: We have a small garden behind the house.
The children are playing in the garden.

meanings.note: Used with right and left: الجهة اليمين 'the right side', من هاي الجهة 'from this side'.

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the other side.
Walk this way, it is closer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجهز, بيجهز).

examples.trans: We prepared the quiet attic room for you.
Salma got breakfast ready early.

meanings.note: Refers to both weather and the emotional vibe of a room (ألطف الجو 'lighten the mood').

examples.trans: The mood is a bit tense today.
The weather is nice in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun for an answer or musical response (plural: أجوبة).

examples.trans: A breath first and a second answer on the key.
We are waiting for an answer from City Hall tomorrow.

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جوعانة, plural: جوعانين).

examples.trans: Eight hungry guests are coming down to breakfast.
Come eat, you look hungry.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for a pocket or hollow recess (جيب الطوب 'the brick pocket'). Plural: جيوب.

examples.text: هداك الجيب تحت الحجرة مبطن بطوب.
examples.trans: That pocket under the stone is lined with brick.
He put the small key in the coat pocket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جيب.

examples.trans: Put the key in the coat pocket.
The paper is in my right pocket.

meanings.note: Active participle of حب used for polite wishes; with كنت (كنت حابة هيك) it means 'I would have loved that'.

examples.trans: I would have loved to sit with you.
I really like the idea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حواجب.

examples.trans: Why did you knit your eyebrows like that?
He raised his eyebrow in surprise.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for an incident or mishap (حادثة الملصق المبلول 'the soggy poster accident'). Plural: حوادث.

examples.text: حتى حادثة الملصق صارت موضة بالشارع!
examples.trans: Even the poster accident became a street trend!

examples.text: هاي حادثة صغيرة وخلصت على خير.
examples.trans: That was a small mishap and ended well.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: Form III verb from حساب: رح نحاسبهم ('we will make them answer for what they did').

examples.trans: The principal will hold everyone accountable.
We must hold them accountable for their mistake.

meanings.note: Active participle of حس ('to feel'), used in spoken Jordanian for present state ('I feel').

examples.trans: I feel I will sleep well tonight.

examples.text: حاسس إنه اليوم رح يكون حلو.
examples.trans: I have a feeling today will be lovely.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة حاسيتها.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing حاسيتها.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على حاسيتها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with حاسيتها.

meanings.note: Active participle of حط ('to put, place').

examples.trans: Mazen has put old boxes on the stairs.
What have you packed inside this suitcase?

meanings.note: Feminine noun for the rim of a tin or the edge of a paving stone (الحافة الشمالية 'the north edge'). Plural: حواف.

examples.trans: We wrapped white tape around the rim of the tin.
Lower the north edge first gently.

meanings.note: With possessive endings, حال acts as 'myself/yourself/itself' (لحاله by itself, لا تغلبي حالك don't tire yourself).

examples.trans: The door opened by itself from the wind.
How are you doing today?

meanings.note: Adverb 'at the moment, for now'.

examples.trans: For now, the suitcase is safe and sound in the closet.
Currently the tables serve the inn's guests.

meanings.note: From ح-م-ل ('to carry, hold'); names a music stand (حامل النوتة) or lamp/book holder.

examples.text: حطينا الورقة على حامل النوتة الخشب.
examples.trans: We set the sheet on the wooden music stand.

examples.text: حامل المفاتيح معلق ورا مكتب الاستقبال.
examples.trans: The key rack hangs behind the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحاول, بيحاول).

examples.trans: I tried to smile as hard as I could!
We tried to find a quick solution.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحب, بيحب).

examples.trans: I liked working here so much more!
Would you like coffee or black tea?

meanings.note: Everyday counting unit for rolls of bread, fruit, lemons, or pills (خدي حبة take a piece; ست حبات ليمون six lemons).

examples.trans: Take a bread roll while it is hot.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحبار.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Form I verb (بحبس / حبس). Used literally for confining or playfully when rain traps someone indoors.

examples.text: أسبوع شتا حبس المسافر بغرفة تمانية.
examples.trans: A rainy week trapped the traveller in Room Eight.

examples.text: المطر حبسنا جوا القاعة طول الصبح.
examples.trans: The rain kept us inside the hall all morning.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural حبال (hibaal).

examples.trans: Pull the rope tight on the tree.
We tied the lanterns with a sturdy cord.

meanings.note: Used warmly across ages in Jordan: يا حبيبي (to a boy/man, or as 'my goodness!') and يا حبيبتي (to a girl/woman).

examples.trans: Good morning, my dear.
A warm welcome to dear friends.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة حبيبتيفي.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing حبيبتيفي.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على حبيبتيفي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with حبيبتيفي.

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة حجار.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing حجار.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على حجار.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with حجار.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجار.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حجرية, plural: حجريين).

examples.trans: Go down the stone stairs to downtown.
She stood beside the stone fountain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجوزات.

examples.trans: I have a booking for a double room.
I read the booking ledger in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة حد.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing حد.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على حد.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with حد.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'someone / anyone'; with ما في (ما في حدا) it means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eleven' (حدعش وتلت 'twenty past eleven').

examples.trans: It is twenty past eleven now.
We counted ten, eleven, twelve.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حديثة, plural: حديثين).

examples.trans: We installed a modern hot-water system.
The building is old, yet the service is modern.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The iron gate is locked at night.
Pass me the heavy iron wrench.

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian feminine noun for a public park or walled garden (حدائق 'parks').

examples.trans: The park bench is painted beside the arch.

examples.text: بنتمشى بالحديقة كل يوم جمعة العصر.
examples.trans: We walk in the park every Friday afternoon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحذية.

examples.trans: Take off your shoes by the door.
Inside the bag are two pairs of men's shoes.

meanings.note: Feminine noun sharing its root with حذاء ('shoe'). Plural: حذوات.

examples.trans: An iron horseshoe is very heavy.

examples.text: علقوا حذوة قديمة فوق باب الورشة.
examples.trans: They hung an old horseshoe above the workshop door.

meanings.note: From ح-ر-ر ('hot, warm'); describes warmth retained by clay cups or weather temperature.

examples.text: الفخار السميك بيحفظ حرارة الشاي وقت طويل.
examples.trans: Thick pottery holds the heat of the tea for a long time.
The oven temperature is ideal for morning bread.

meanings.note: In Jordanian household speech, حرام (plural حرامات) is the everyday word for a warm bed blanket.

examples.trans: I have a warm wool blanket on the bed.
We brought clean blankets from the closet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حروف.

examples.trans: Two small letters are written on the corner.
The letters of her name are clear on the zip.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for an artisanal craft or profession. Plural: حرف (حرف يدوية 'handicrafts').

examples.text: بالمهرجان في طاولات حرف يدوية حلوة.
examples.trans: At the festival there are lovely local craft tables.

examples.text: رسم الخرايط حرفة بدها صبر ودقة.
examples.trans: Mapmaking is a craft that requires patience and precision.

meanings.note: Transitive Form II verb ('move furniture, stir a pot, wiggle toes').

examples.text: حركنا البيانو خطوتين لورا بعيد عن الشباك.
examples.trans: We moved the piano two steps back away from the window.

examples.text: حركي الشوربة بملعقة خشب كل خمس دقايق.
examples.trans: Stir the soup with a wooden spoon every five minutes.

meanings.note: In the plural حركات, often means 'attitude / games / antics' (بطلي حركاتك الباردة).

examples.trans: I don't like these antics.
I noticed every move she made.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحزر, بيحزر).

examples.trans: Let me guess what happened!
She guessed the answer on the first try.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحس, بيحس).

examples.text: نتمنى كل ضيف يحس بالراحة هون.
examples.trans: We hope every guest feels at home here.
I felt the warmth the moment I walked in.

meanings.note: Also used in the warm hospitality phrase على حسابنا ('on our tab / on the house').

examples.trans: The bill is thirty-eight dinars.
The first coffee today is on the house!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة حساباتي.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing حساباتي.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على حساباتي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with حساباتي.

meanings.note: Used idiomatically in بحسب إلها ألف حساب ('takes her very seriously / fears crossing her').

examples.trans: We calculated the time exactly.
Count me in with you.

meanings.note: Form II causative of حس ('to feel'). حسّسني بدفا means 'made me feel warm'.

examples.text: ولا مكان حسّسني بدفا أكتر من هون.
examples.trans: No place ever made me feel warmer than here.
Your kind words made me feel at ease.

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic word for horse. Plural: أحصنة or خيل.

examples.trans: The horse runs fast across the plain.
We drew a small horse on the paper.

meanings.note: Respectful Jordanian way to say 'you' to a guest or elder (hadritak to a man, hadritik to a woman).

examples.trans: You must be Mr. Rami.
Please, what would you like to drink?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun (حظ حلو 'good luck'). Plural: حظوظ.

examples.text: دق الحجرة دقة وحدة عشان الحظ الحلو!
examples.trans: Tap the stone once for good luck!

examples.text: من حسن الحظ لقينا المفتاح بدرج المكتب.
examples.trans: By good luck we found the key in the desk drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة حفة.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing حفة.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على حفة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with حفة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة حفته.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing حفته.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على حفته.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with حفته.

حفر.gloss: to carve; wear a groove in

meanings.en: to carve; wear a groove in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحفر, بيحفر).

examples.text: احكي معه قبل ما يحفر خشب الأرضية!
examples.trans: Talk to him before he wears a groove in the floorboards!
My grandfather carved the wooden train by hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على خمس.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with خمس.

meanings.note: Numeral 'five'; short form خمس (khams) before a plural noun (خمس دقايق 'five minutes').

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fifteen' before a counted noun (خمستعشر سنة 'fifteen years').

examples.trans: I have not seen it in fifteen years!
The landing is after fifteen steps.

meanings.note: Numeral 'fifty'.

examples.trans: Here is fifty dinars from the cash box.
She saved fifty piastres on the bill.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة خميل.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing خميل.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على خميل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with خميل.

meanings.note: Form II causative verb (khawwaf) from خاف: خوفتيني ('you startled me'), أخوفك ('scare you').

examples.trans: You honestly startled me when you walked in!
I didn't mean to scare you.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian speech, خيال commonly means a cast 'shadow' or 'silhouette' as well as 'imagination'.

examples.text: شفت خيال القطة على الحيط تحت الفانوس.
examples.trans: I saw the cat's shadow on the wall beneath the lantern.

examples.text: خيال الشجرة واصل لحد باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: The tree's shadow reaches right to the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for something.

examples.text: هذه جملة طويلة كفاية لكي لا تكون قصيرة جدا وتحتوي على كلمة خيط.
examples.trans: This is a long enough sentence so it is not too short, containing خيط.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على خيط.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with خيط.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) disambiguated with fatha-sukun from noun خُبز ('bread').

examples.text: ريحة الخبز الطازة رح تعبي الساحة من الصبح.
examples.trans: The smell of fresh baking will fill the courtyard from early morning.

examples.text: وقت الخبز بالفرن عشرين دقيقة بالتمام.
examples.trans: The baking time in the oven is twenty minutes sharp.

خِلِص.gloss: to run out; be finished; end

meanings.en: to run out; be finished; end
meanings.note: Form I intransitive counterpart of transitive خلّص ('to finish something'): خلص الخبز means 'the bread has run out'.

examples.text: يلا نمشي قبل ما يخلص الخبز السخن.
examples.trans: Let's walk over before the hot bread sells out.

examples.text: خلصت القهوة، رح أعمل إبريق جديد.
examples.trans: The coffee ran out; I will make a fresh pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دوائر.

examples.trans: A paper arrived from the property department.
The department office is downtown.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دائمة, plural: دائمين).

examples.trans: She became the permanent reception manager at the guesthouse.
He wrote it in the ledger in permanent ink.

meanings.note: Active participle of دخل ('to enter'), used like a progressive verb in Arabic (بيت الياسمين داخل على المهرجان 'is entering the festival').

examples.text: بيت الياسمين داخل على مهرجان الساحات!
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is entering the Courtyard Festival!

examples.text: هي سعاد داخلة من باب الساحة.
examples.trans: Look, Suad is coming in through the courtyard door.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian verb meaning 'to manage, run (a shop/inn)' and in دير بالك ('take care!').

examples.text: عمتي كانت تدير قاعة الشاي لحالها.
examples.trans: My aunt used to run the tea room on her own.

examples.text: مازن بيدير النزل مع طارق ونور وسلمى.
examples.trans: Mazen runs the inn with Tariq, Nour, and Salma.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافعة, plural: دافعين).

examples.text: ما بدنا نزعج ضيف دافع حق غرفته.
examples.trans: We do not want to bother a paying guest.
All the guests have paid the bill in advance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine hollow verb (from Classical ذاق, with ذ -> د); imperative دوق / دوقي ('taste!').

examples.text: دوقي هالمربى الحلو قبل ما نشتري المرطبان.
examples.trans: Taste this sweet jam before we buy the jar.
Ziad tasted the honey and smiled right away.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of دائما ('always').

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.
Noon traffic is always slow.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine pronunciation (daayman) of classical دائماً.

examples.trans: She always comes early.
We always sit here.

meanings.note: Small metal pin, tack, or brass hinge pivot pin.

examples.text: دبوس المفصلة النحاس صغير كتير وبده ملقط.
examples.trans: The brass hinge pin is tiny and requires tweezers.

examples.text: علقت الورقة على اللوح بدبوس صغير.
examples.trans: I pinned the note onto the board with a small tack.

دخل.gloss: to enter; come in; go in

meanings.en: to enter; come in; go in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدخل, بيدخل).

examples.text: تفضل ادخل من المطر يا أستاذ.
examples.trans: Please come in out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of دخل ('to enter'). تسجيل دخول means 'check-in' at a hotel or guesthouse.

examples.text: كل ضيف بيسجل دخول بيشوف الخريطة.
